title: 6-round AES-128: direct sum, five-byte filter for selected subkey recovery

target.description: AES-128 reduced to 6 rounds on 128-bit blocks; initial AddRoundKey k^(0), then rounds 1 through 6, with no MixColumns in the final round. The filter recovers four selected bytes of k^(6) and one selected byte of the equivalent key k'^(5)=MixColumns^-1(k^(5)): 40 bits of subkey material.

setting.key_relation: One unknown master key with the standard AES expansion; no related-key access.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: Six chosen-plaintext structures, each varying the four bytes feeding one first-round column over all 2^32 possibilities and fixing the other bytes.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.

The paper presents these constructions as attacks on Rijndael. This record prices the explicitly analyzed selected-subkey filter; complete master-key reconstruction and any repeated filter applications are left for a separate completion-budget review.
All three AES key lengths share this round-subkey filter; the procedure does not itself determine a complete master key.

time.note: Section 2.3 first analyzes direct evaluation of Equation (1): 2^32 ciphertexts times 2^40 guesses gives 2^72 elementary evaluations, estimated as 2^64 trial encryptions. Additional structures filter surviving guesses; no separate coefficient is supplied.

memory.note: Section 2.3 evaluates four selected bytes from the input ciphertext list; it does not state a complete peak-memory count for direct summation.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: Later-source-derived lower bound within the repeated uniform 8-bit wrong-tuple-filter model for the unique correct complete five-byte subkey output. The original construction checks six complete 2^32-plaintext structures; exact direct evaluation and parity-preserving partial sums compute the same XOR and retain the true tuple. DGKLMM2024 explicitly reanalyzes this FKLSSWW2001 construction, the same five selected bytes, and six structures. In that source model each wrong tuple survives all six tests with probability 2^-48, so E_model W < 2^40*2^-48=2^-8 and the first-moment bound gives P_model >= 255/256. No independence between different wrong tuples is required. Repeated-test uniformity/independence remains a source-model assumption, not a proved actual-AES joint law. This is not an author-printed aggregate percentage, an empirical rate, or full-master-key recovery. Original data, operation units and costs are preserved; the later refined operation count is not transplanted.

review.scope: Verified original/later exact-edition mapping, same five-byte output and six-structure budget, exact correct-tuple retention, and conditional model first-moment inference. Independent source-first and endpoint review. This does not verify actual-cipher repeated-filter assumptions, attack reproduction, full-master-key completion or a new full-paper audit.
